title: introduce-rotary-stride-prefetch-quantized-attn-orchestrator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR introduces a coordinated set of changes to the attention execution path focused on reducing tail latency and improving throughput for medium- and long-context workloads. We observed KV cache pressure and prefetch stalls for workloads with irregular rotary/rope offsets (long context + many short requests interleaved). The design goal is to make prefetched KV ranges stride-aware and to expose a quantized microkernel path that reduces memory bandwidth and occupancy on Ampere/next-gen GPUs.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a Rotary Stride Prefetch orchestrator that computes contiguous prefetch windows using stride heuristics instead of simple prefix-only heuristics; this reduces wasted prefetch and IO contention when rotary offsets vary across requests.
- Introduces a small quantized attention microkernel (int8-aware FP16 accumulation path) that runs when model/weight quantization profiles are compatible. The microkernel sacrifices a small amount of peak accuracy (controlled via guard rails) for a 20–30% effective throughput improvement on our perf harness for 8k context runs.
- Adds cooperative scheduling hooks so the continuous batcher can split hot keys across the new prefetch windows and avoid blocking the global KV commit.
- Adds metrics, tracing spans, and an opt-in runtime flag (--enable-rotary-stride-prefetch) to control rollout.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Rotary stride prefetch algorithm implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Quantized microkernel with accuracy guard and unit tests
- [x] Scheduler integration and continuous-batcher tests
- [x] End-to-end perf harness and CI benchmark added
- [x] Docs: performance notes and rollout instructions added

Performance summary (internal benchmark on p4d.24xlarge, FP16/INT8 mix tests):
- Throughput: +22% median tokens/s for mixed short+long workloads (4k–8k).
- P99 latency: -18% on average for batched streaming scenarios with rotary variance.
- KV memory traffic: ~15% reduction in peak bytes/sec due to reduced redundant prefetch.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag; default remains previous behavior.
- Runtime detects mismatch between quantization profile and model weights; it falls back to the FP16 path automatically.
- Added end-to-end regression checks using saved prompt sets to ensure text-quality delta < 0.2% (ROUGE-like) for models in our curated catalog.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for stride heuristics and window generation (serving/attn/tests/stride_prefetch_test.rs).
- Microkernel correctness tests (serving/attn/kernels/quant_tile_test.cu).
- Integration tests in continuous-batcher harness and perf CI (benchmarks/attn/rotary_stride_perf.yaml).
- Manual validation on dedicated cluster mirrors of customer workload (summary attached in the commit).

Rollout plan:
- Canary on Dedicated pools with --enable-rotary-stride-prefetch=false by default. Gradual enablement via per-customer config.
- Monitor new metrics: attn.prefetch.window_utilization, attn.quant.path_rate, attn.kv.prefetch_reductions.

Related work and followups:
- This PR is complementary to ENG-1320 (adaptive batching heuristics) and will be followed by a separate change to integrate with the eviction policy (ENG-1256).

Notes on implementation choices:
- Chose stride heuristics (local median stride + hot-key amplification) because simple prefix caching caused repeated overfetch for interleaved short sessions.
- Quantized microkernel targets the common weight layout we onboarded earlier; it uses fused matmul-rotary + scaled accumulation to minimize warp divergence.

Merge notes:
- CI had one flaky throughput test on the first run; rerun fixed it. All checks green at merge.

review_comments: Ravi Patel (2025-11-22): Nice design. Two requests: please add a microbenchmark comparing the old prefetch vs stride-prefetch on synthetic hot-key patterns, and clarify the fallback path where quantization is incompatible.

Elena Grigorev (2025-11-25): Found a possible race between batcher split and KV commit; suggested moving the prefetch completion signal behind the KV commit future. Also request small API doc for the new metrics.
Maya Chen (2025-11-26): Fixed the ordering in continuous_batcher.rs and added metric docs. PTAL.
Samir Kapoor (2025-11-28): Ran canary on a dedicated pool; observed improved throughput but one workload showed a 1.2% quality regression — tracked as ENG-1375. Approved with follow-up.

release_notes: Adds a rotary-stride prefetch orchestrator and an opt-in quantized attention microkernel. Improves throughput for mixed-length workloads and reduces KV prefetch waste. Feature gated and off by default. See docs/perf/rotary_stride_prefetch.md for rollout instructions.
